question: What proportion of infertility cases are attributed to male factors?
explanation: Male factors contribute to roughly half of all documented infertility cases globally and locally. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h1)

question: Why is joint evaluation important for infertile couples in Nigerian clinical practice?

options.A: It ensures only the male partner receives treatment
options.B: It reduces cultural stigma and shares the diagnostic burden
options.C: It is legally required by hospital management boards
options.D: It eliminates the need for expensive laboratory tests

explanation: Evaluating both partners together helps combat the cultural bias that unfairly blames women for childlessness. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h1)

question: Where does spermatogenesis primarily take place inside the testes?
explanation: Sperm production occurs specifically within the specialized seminiferous tubules of the testes. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h2)

question: Which hormone directly stimulates Leydig cells to produce testosterone?
explanation: Luteinizing hormone targets the interstitial Leydig cells to synthesize and secrete testosterone. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h2)

question: How do pre-testicular factors primarily impair male fertility?

options.A: By disrupting hormonal signals from the brain to the testes
options.B: By causing physical blockages in the vas deferens
options.C: By creating antibodies that destroy mature sperm cells
options.D: By elevating scrotal temperature above normal body levels

explanation: Pre-testicular causes involve central endocrine failures that prevent proper stimulation of the testes. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h3)

question: Which condition is a well-known pre-testicular cause of male infertility?
explanation: This condition involves low gonadotropins from the brain, leading to deficient testosterone and sperm production. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h3)

question: What is the term for undescended testes that can lead to infertility?
explanation: Cryptorchidism describes the failure of one or both testes to descend into the scrotal sac. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h4)

question: How does a varicocele negatively affect sperm production in the testes?

options.A: By blocking the urethra during ejaculation
options.B: By increasing blood pooling and raising scrotal temperature
options.C: By causing severe systemic bacterial infections
options.D: By destroying pituitary gland hormone receptors

explanation: Varicoceles disrupt normal venous drainage, warming the testes and impairing spermatogenesis. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h4)

question: What is obstructive azoospermia characterized by?

options.A: Absence of sperm in semen due to a physical blockage
options.B: Complete absence of testicular tissue from birth
options.C: Total failure of the pituitary gland to release hormones
options.D: Genetic mutation on the twenty-first chromosome

explanation: Testes produce sperm, but physical obstructions prevent them from entering the ejaculate. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h5)

question: What is a common infectious cause of post-testicular ductal obstruction in Nigeria?
explanation: Unmanaged infections lead to inflammatory strictures along the delicate male reproductive tract. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h5)

question: Which lifestyle habit generates reactive oxygen species that damage sperm DNA?
explanation: Tobacco smoke introduces toxins and oxidative stress that degrade sperm integrity. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h6)

question: Why does prolonged exposure to high scrotal temperatures impair male fertility?

options.A: Normal spermatogenesis requires a temperature slightly cooler than body core temperature
options.B: High heat directly destroys the pituitary gland in the brain
options.C: Elevated temperatures stop the prostate gland from producing fluid
options.D: Heat causes immediate permanent closure of the seminal vesicles

explanation: The testes hang outside the body because optimal sperm production requires a cooler environment. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h6)

question: What is the recommended period of sexual abstinence before collecting a semen sample?
explanation: Standard guidelines require a brief abstinence window to ensure reliable sperm concentration and volume measurements. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of a semen analysis in clinical evaluation?

options.A: To detect active bacterial infections in the kidneys
options.B: To diagnose underlying genetic mutations in chromosomes
options.C: To measure circulating testosterone levels in the blood
options.D: To assess sperm concentration, motility, and morphology

explanation: Semen analysis provides direct laboratory data on the physical and functional characteristics of sperm. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h7)

question: What surgical procedure is commonly performed to repair an enlarged scrotal vein plexus?
explanation: Varicocelectomy is the surgical correction of a varicocele to improve testicular environment and sperm parameters. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h8)

question: When are assisted reproductive technologies like intracytoplasmic sperm injection recommended?

options.A: As the absolute first-line treatment for every mild hormonal imbalance
options.B: To permanently prevent future pregnancies in young men
options.C: Only when the female partner has no reproductive organs
options.D: When medical and surgical treatments fail to resolve severe infertility

explanation: Advanced assisted reproduction bridges the gap when direct corrective measures cannot restore natural fertility. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h8)

question: Which psychological response is commonly experienced by couples facing infertility?
explanation: The prolonged stress of trying to conceive frequently leads to significant emotional distress and mood disorders. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h9)

question: How can nurses best assist couples dealing with the social stigma of male infertility?

options.A: By offering a confidential, non-judgmental space for open dialogue
options.B: By advising immediate separation and divorce
options.C: By publicly disclosing diagnostic results to extended family members
options.D: By discouraging them from seeking any professional counseling

explanation: Creating a supportive clinical atmosphere empowers couples to cope with societal pressures and share their feelings safely. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h9)
